findings.impact: An incomplete or spoofed conditional report could cause affected tests to be skipped because the consumer never checks a context dependency.
findings.text: The v2 contract says requirements are mandatory and missing requirements fail closed, but defines only the kinds and values that the schema permits, not an independently defined complete requirement set and evidence binding for each allowlisted model/version and relevant input. A malformed report can omit a loader/hook requirement while retaining a nonempty unique requirements list, or substitute a weaker evidence kind; a consumer checking only present entries has no way to recognize the omission and may select sparsely without establishing the required context. Require an independent, versioned model contract for required IDs/kinds and admissible evidence bindings, including requirements triggered by discovered input; compare the report against it and fall back on missing, substituted, inconsistent or unknown entries. Test removal, evidence-kind substitution and omission of input-triggered requirements.

output.summary: Independent model registry and evidence binding resolve the requirement-completeness finding.
Approved portable commit-only analysis and committed symlink handling.

responses.review_design:8:1: fixed: Replaced fabricated expected execution values with machine-readable registered predicates, concrete inventory and baseline descriptors and independent G2 binding; added standalone-to-G2 success and forged/mismatched evidence tests.

output.summary: Separate standalone analyzer predicates and commit-derived parameters from runtime facts collected by G2. Bind and validate the actual profile, inventory and baseline through independently registered collectors before using a conditional sparse result.

Adversarial review resolved the registry completeness finding. The design review identified one material issue: execution-only values must be bound by the consumer or supplied through a supported context input. That issue reopens design. No non-material notes require verdicts.

Re-review retains the material changed-tree fallback issue and identifies two material cache issues: ESM parser runtime identity and Windows permission handling. These reopen implementation. No non-material notes require verdicts.

findings.text: The owner approved schema v2 with explicit conditional status, versioned supported-model identity and mandatory machine-readable execution-context requirements, while retaining conservative v1 fallback. Update this design and dependent G2 design before implementation: specify exact v2 CLI/schema selection and status, tracked-source Node/TypeScript dependency model and its boundaries, mandatory runtime/runner/loader/environment requirements and their evidence, fail-closed rules for unknown or unmet conditions, validation and backward compatibility; require a concrete sparse two-target fixture plus adversarial dynamic loader, plugin, resource, fixture and import-side-effect cases. Quote the owner decision recorded on implement attempt 7. An unverified conditional report must never be consumed as unconditional completeness.

output.summary: Preserved the ESM runtime identity and Windows ACL cache changes at 39f6612. All three existing contract suites passed on Linux; Windows ACL behavior still requires real Windows verification. The owner-approved conditional schema requires a design and test revision before sparse execution can be implemented safely.

findings.impact: The analyzer cannot construct a valid usable conditional report for its stated CLI, so practical sparse execution may be impossible or require unverifiable guessed expectations.
findings.text: The v2 report requires an `expected` value for each singleton including actual runner/profile, discovered inventory and compatible baseline receipt identity, but the documented `trail impact` invocation provides only two commit arguments and schema version; G1 cannot determine which G2 profile, inventory or local receipt will be used. Define a machine-readable registry predicate/descriptor for execution-only facts that G2 independently binds and verifies, or a supported explicit context input with strict validation, and distinguish analyzer-known facts from consumer evidence. Test standalone analyzer invocation followed by a real matching G2 conditional sparse run and forged/mismatched values.

not: A new graph service, a replacement test runner or a separately implemented multilingual parser.

principles: Test selection and execution require no model reasoning during normal runs.
intent.purpose: Determine which tests to run based on a git changeset.
intent.serves: Developers, CI, and agents performing repeated unit and integration test runs during development.

output.summary: Define how standalone analyzer requirements express execution-only context values.

findings.impact: The report can validate and cache analysis of a different source tree than the exact commit requested.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts Git commands honor replace refs: a requested commit ID can be paired with a different commit’s tree and replacement blob bytes. Disable replacement effects or verify real objects for every endpoint/tree/blob read.

findings.impact: The analyzer cannot enable sparse execution for any normal repository, even with identical endpoints and a compatible passing baseline.
findings.response: disputed: Identical populated Git trees now analyze inputs and return complete when no actual gaps exist. Changed trees still require unbounded fallback because callbacks, resources, dynamic dispatch and cross-file resolution remain unmodeled; treating those relationships as complete would violate the approved design. No unsupported scope is claimed.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts unconditionally emits an unbounded gap for every changed tree and every identical nonempty tree. Implement justified supported completeness or bounded scopes, including a valid unchanged populated tree, rather than always forcing full-profile fallback.

findings.impact: Normal installations report an indistinguishable unavailable grammar identity and always disable extraction caching, undermining reproducibility and repeated-run performance.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts derives grammar identity and the raw extraction cache key from package-lock.json, but package.json excludes this file from the npm distribution. Use shipped actual grammar identities and enable safe extraction cache reuse in installed packages.

findings.impact: The current test suite passes while exact identity can be falsified and sparse execution and production cache reuse never occur.
findings.text: test/conservative-impact-contract.test.ts checks valid empty only for empty repositories and lacks replacement-ref and actual packed-install checks. Add regression coverage for immutable commit/tree/blob IDs under Git replacements, unchanged populated trees without fabricated full fallback, and installed package grammar identity/cache reuse.

findings.impact: A changed ESM parser runtime can retain the same grammar identity and cache key, replaying extraction facts from a different runtime.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts grammarIdentity hashes createRequire.resolve("web-tree-sitter"), the CJS entrypoint, but src/graph/wasm-runtime.ts dynamically imports the distinct ESM entrypoint web-tree-sitter.js for breadth/container parsing. Hash the actual loaded runtime or otherwise version all parsing inputs.

findings.impact: The required extraction cache is unavailable on a supported platform, hurting repeated-run performance and breaking the packaged distribution test there.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts extractionCache tests POSIX group/other mode bits on all platforms. On Windows libuv synthesizes those bits for ordinary writable directories and does not model NTFS ACL privacy, so the parent check rejects cache creation and the packed cache test fails. Use a Windows-appropriate secure cache design and verify on Windows.

output.summary: Changed comparisons still force full fallback; Windows cache permissions and the grammar runtime identity also require correction.

findings.text: The packed-package test builds from git archive HEAD rather than the current checkout. Running npm test after an uncommitted implementation or package metadata edit can test an old distribution, hiding new regressions or falsely reporting a fixed defect. Materialize a safe isolated copy of the actual current test source (including relevant modified and added inputs), while retaining offline dependencies and protecting concurrent tests from shared build outputs.

output.summary: Isolated source copy now includes current checkout edits and additions; remaining finding resolved.

spec: Implement conservative impact analysis directly in this Trail-code fork specified in docs/test-impact/design.md, sections 1–6, 8, 11–13 and delivery steps 1–2. Use upstream base ca20a67764e99531a1cf272eea8354e2c16f71d9 and define versioned impact contracts and exact explicit endpoints. Analyze both snapshots, preserve ambiguity and analysis gaps, traverse complete reverse dependencies without arbitrary limits, handle deletions, renames and rebinding, and isolate and validate conservative caches. Report justified fallback scopes instead of silently omitting uncertainty. Include meaningful tests for endpoint semantics, graph completeness, gaps, cache freshness and representative dependency cases. Preserve upstream licensing and document the pinned source. Do not implement a replacement parser or assume normal navigation output is conservative. The full design and its acceptance matrix are binding; resolve open distribution and interface choices through the workflow. Work directly in this fork for a future upstream pull request; no separate test-impact repository or Git subtree. Preserve the separate Unity plugin branch. Where the design refers to a separate fork and adapter distribution, adapt it to this unified repository. Owner scope clarification: Initial release requires explicit committed Git endpoints only, and must work across platforms and filesystems with ordinary Git repositories, without Btrfs, privileged operations, special mounts or subvolumes. Worktree target support is deferred; reject it clearly rather than silently substituting a commit. Preserve exact target execution identity and protection against mutations, and adapt the original worktree-specific acceptance cases accordingly.
title: Build conservative two-snapshot impact analysis
